name: Derivative of a vector-valued function
description: For a function f mapping an interval of R into a normed vector space E, the derivative at a point x₀ is the limit of (f(x) - f(x₀))/(x - x₀) as x → x₀, when this limit exists in E.

name: Differentiability
description: A function f is differentiable at x₀ if there exists a continuous linear map L such that f(x₀ + h) = f(x₀) + L(h) + o(h) as h → 0.

name: Linearity of differentiation
description: The derivative operator is linear: (αf + βg)' = αf' + βg' for differentiable functions f, g and scalars α, β.

name: Product rule (Leibniz rule)
description: If f and g are differentiable real-valued functions, then (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

name: Chain rule
description: If g is differentiable at x₀ and f is differentiable at g(x₀), then f ∘ g is differentiable at x₀ with derivative f'(g(x₀)) · g'(x₀).

name: Derivative of the inverse function
description: If f is a continuous bijection differentiable at x₀ with f'(x₀) ≠ 0, then f⁻¹ is differentiable at f(x₀) with derivative 1/f'(x₀).

name: Monotonicity criterion via derivative
description: A differentiable function f on an interval is non-decreasing if and only if f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

name: Convexity criterion via second derivative
description: A twice-differentiable function f on an interval is convex if and only if f''(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

name: Higher-order derivative
description: The n-th derivative f⁽ⁿ⁾ is defined inductively as the derivative of f⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, when it exists.

name: Leibniz formula for n-th derivative of a product
description: The n-th derivative of a product fg equals Σₖ₌₀ⁿ C(n,k) f⁽ᵏ⁾g⁽ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁾.

name: Regulated function
description: A function f from an interval I into a Banach space E is regulated if it has a left limit and a right limit at every point of I, equivalently if it is a uniform limit of step functions.

name: Step function
description: A function on an interval that takes only finitely many values, each on a sub-interval of a finite partition.

name: Integral of a regulated function
description: The integral of a regulated function f is defined as the limit of integrals of step functions converging uniformly to f, and this limit is independent of the approximating sequence.

name: Primitive (antiderivative)
description: A primitive of a function f on an interval I is a function F such that F' = f on I.

name: Integration by parts
description: If f and g are continuously differentiable on [a,b], then ∫ₐᵇ f'(t)g(t) dt = f(b)g(b) - f(a)g(a) - ∫ₐᵇ f(t)g'(t) dt.

name: Change of variables in integrals
description: If φ is a C¹ diffeomorphism and f is regulated, then ∫_{φ(a)}^{φ(b)} f(t) dt = ∫ₐᵇ f(φ(u)) φ'(u) du.

name: Integral remainder for Taylor's formula
description: If f is of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder in the n-th order Taylor expansion equals (1/n!) ∫₀ʰ (h-t)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀+t) dt.

name: Uniform convergence and integration
description: If a sequence of regulated functions converges uniformly to f, then f is regulated and the integral of the limit equals the limit of the integrals.

name: Improper integral (convergent integral on unbounded interval)
description: The integral ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt is defined as limₓ→∞ ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt when this limit exists.

name: Absolute convergence of improper integrals
description: If ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt converges, then ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt converges and ‖∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt‖ ≤ ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt.

name: Power function x^α
description: For x > 0 and α ∈ R, defined as x^α = exp(α log x), extending integer powers to all real exponents.

name: Number π
description: Defined as twice the smallest positive zero of cosine, establishing the period 2π of the trigonometric functions.

name: Inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan)
description: The inverse functions of sin, cos, tan restricted to appropriate intervals where they are bijective, with derivatives 1/√(1-x²), -1/√(1-x²), 1/(1+x²) respectively.

name: Hyperbolic functions (sinh, cosh, tanh)
description: Defined as sinh(x) = (eˣ - e⁻ˣ)/2, cosh(x) = (eˣ + e⁻ˣ)/2, tanh(x) = sinh(x)/cosh(x), satisfying the identity cosh²(x) - sinh²(x) = 1.

name: Inverse hyperbolic functions
description: The inverses of sinh, cosh|[0,∞), tanh, expressible in terms of logarithm: arsinh(x) = log(x + √(x²+1)).

name: Analyticity of elementary functions
description: The functions exp, log, sin, cos, and their inverses are all real-analytic on their domains of definition, represented by convergent power series.

name: Growth comparison of elementary functions
description: As x → +∞, for any α > 0 and β > 0: (log x)^α = o(x^β) and x^β = o(e^{αx}), establishing the asymptotic hierarchy log ≪ polynomial ≪ exponential.

name: Lipschitz condition
description: A function f(t, y) satisfies a Lipschitz condition in y if ‖f(t, y₁) - f(t, y₂)‖ ≤ K‖y₁ - y₂‖ for some constant K and all (t, yᵢ) in the domain.

name: Integral equation formulation of ODE
description: The initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t₀) = y₀ is equivalent to the integral equation y(t) = y₀ + ∫_{t₀}^t f(s, y(s)) ds.

name: Maximal solution of an ODE
description: A solution defined on a maximal interval of existence that cannot be extended to a larger interval, whose existence is guaranteed by Zorn's lemma from local solutions.

name: Blow-up criterion (escape to boundary)
description: If the maximal interval of existence of a solution is bounded, then the solution leaves every compact subset of the domain of f, i.e., ‖y(t)‖ → ∞ or the solution approaches the boundary.

name: Linear ordinary differential equation
description: An ODE of the form y' = A(t)y + b(t), where A(t) is a continuous matrix-valued function and b(t) is continuous, whose solutions form an affine subspace.

name: Homogeneous linear ODE
description: A linear ODE of the form y' = A(t)y (with b = 0) whose solutions form a vector space of dimension equal to the order of the system.

name: Fundamental matrix (resolvent)
description: A matrix-valued function Φ(t) whose columns form a basis of solutions of y' = A(t)y, satisfying Φ' = A(t)Φ with Φ(t₀) = I.

name: Variation of constants (variation of parameters)
description: A method to solve the non-homogeneous equation y' = A(t)y + b(t) by writing y(t) = Φ(t)c(t) where Φ is the fundamental matrix, leading to c'(t) = Φ(t)⁻¹b(t).

name: Linear ODE with constant coefficients
description: The system y' = Ay with A constant has the explicit solution y(t) = e^{tA}y₀, reducible via Jordan normal form to exponential-polynomial expressions.

name: Differentiable dependence on parameters
description: If f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in all variables, then the solution y(t, λ) of y' = f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in the parameter λ.

name: Lagrange remainder
description: For f of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder Rₙ(h) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀ + θh) hⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! for some θ ∈ (0,1).

name: Asymptotic expansion
description: A formal series Σ aₙφₙ(x) is an asymptotic expansion of f(x) as x → x₀ if f(x) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ aₖφₖ(x) = o(φₙ(x)) for each n, where (φₙ) is an asymptotic scale.

name: Asymptotic scale
description: A sequence of functions (φₙ) such that φₙ₊₁(x) = o(φₙ(x)) as x → x₀, providing a graded comparison framework for the growth or decay of functions.

name: Little-o and big-O notation
description: f = o(g) means f/g → 0 and f = O(g) means |f/g| is bounded, as x approaches a specified limit, providing a calculus of asymptotic comparison.

name: Asymptotic comparison of functions
description: The systematic use of asymptotic expansions and asymptotic scales to compare functions' growth rates, compute limits of indeterminate forms, and approximate functions near singular points.
function_signature: (Functions near a point) → (Asymptotic ordering and expansions)

name: Bernoulli numbers
description: The sequence of rational numbers Bₙ defined by the generating function t/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ tⁿ/n!, with B₀ = 1, B₁ = -1/2, and B₂ₖ₊₁ = 0 for k ≥ 1.

name: Bernoulli polynomials
description: Polynomials Bₙ(x) defined by the generating function te^{xt}/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ(x) tⁿ/n!, satisfying Bₙ'(x) = nBₙ₋₁(x) and Bₙ(0) = Bₙ.

name: Euler-Maclaurin summation formula
description: Relates a sum Σₖ₌ₐᵇ f(k) to the integral ∫ₐᵇ f(t) dt plus correction terms involving Bernoulli numbers and derivatives of f at the endpoints, with a remainder expressible as an integral involving Bernoulli polynomials.

name: Summation of divergent series by Euler-Maclaurin
description: Using the Euler-Maclaurin formula to assign finite values to formally divergent sums by analytic continuation, yielding values for ζ(-n) in terms of Bernoulli numbers.

name: Asymptotic expansion of the gamma function
description: The Stirling series Γ(x) ~ √(2π) x^{x-1/2} e^{-x} (1 + Σₖ₌₁^∞ cₖ/x^k), an asymptotic expansion for x → +∞ with coefficients expressible via Bernoulli numbers.

name: Beta function
description: Defined as B(p,q) = ∫₀¹ t^{p-1}(1-t)^{q-1} dt for p, q > 0, related to the gamma function by B(p,q) = Γ(p)Γ(q)/Γ(p+q).

name: Digamma function
description: The logarithmic derivative ψ(x) = Γ'(x)/Γ(x) = (d/dx) log Γ(x), whose asymptotic expansion involves Bernoulli numbers: ψ(x) ~ log x - 1/(2x) - Σₖ₌₁^∞ B₂ₖ/(2k·x²ᵏ).

name: Abscissa of convergence
description: The infimum σ₀ of real numbers σ such that the Laplace integral ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} f(t) dt converges, establishing a half-plane Re(s) > σ₀ of convergence.

name: Abscissa of absolute convergence
description: The infimum σₐ of real numbers σ such that ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} |f(t)| dt converges, always satisfying σ₀ ≤ σₐ ≤ σ₀ + 1 for locally integrable f.

name: Laplace transform of derivatives
description: L{f'}(s) = sL{f}(s) - f(0⁺), and more generally L{f⁽ⁿ⁾}(s) = sⁿL{f}(s) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ sⁿ⁻¹⁻ᵏ f⁽ᵏ⁾(0⁺), converting differential equations to algebraic equations.

name: Laplace transform of convolutions
description: L{f * g}(s) = L{f}(s) · L{g}(s), where (f * g)(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f(t-u) g(u) du, converting convolution to pointwise multiplication.

name: Inversion formula for Laplace transform
description: Under suitable conditions, f(t) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c-i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{st} L{f}(s) ds for c > σ₀, recovering f from its Laplace transform via a Bromwich contour integral.

name: Uniqueness theorem for Laplace transform
description: If L{f}(s) = L{g}(s) for all s in a half-plane and f, g are continuous, then f = g, establishing injectivity of the Laplace transform on continuous functions.

name: Application of Laplace transform to linear ODE
description: Converting a linear ODE with constant coefficients and initial conditions to an algebraic equation via Laplace transform, solving algebraically, then inverting to obtain the solution.
function_signature: (Linear ODE with initial conditions) → (Algebraic equation → Solution via inversion)

name: Valued field
description: A field K equipped with an absolute value |·|: K → R₊ satisfying |xy| = |x||y| and the triangle inequality, inducing a metric topology on K.

name: Neighborhood of zero (fundamental system)
description: In a TVS, the topology is entirely determined by a fundamental system of neighborhoods of the origin, which must be absorbing, balanced sets; translations then give the full topology.

name: Absorbing set
description: A subset A of a vector space E such that for every x ∈ E there exists λ₀ > 0 with x ∈ λA for all |λ| ≥ λ₀.

name: Balanced set
description: A subset B of a vector space E such that λB ⊆ B for all scalars λ with |λ| ≤ 1.

name: Bounded set in a TVS
description: A subset B of a TVS E is bounded if for every neighborhood V of 0, there exists λ > 0 such that B ⊆ λV, equivalently if B is absorbed by every neighborhood of zero.

name: Metrizable TVS
description: A TVS whose topology is metrizable, which occurs if and only if it has a countable fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero, in which case it can be metrized by a translation-invariant metric.

name: Normable TVS
description: A TVS whose topology can be defined by a single norm, characterized by having a bounded convex neighborhood of zero.

name: Completeness of a TVS
description: A TVS is complete if every Cauchy net (or Cauchy filter) converges; a complete metrizable locally convex space is a Fréchet space.

name: Topological direct sum of TVS
description: A TVS E is a topological direct sum of subspaces E₁ and E₂ if the map (x₁, x₂) ↦ x₁ + x₂ is a topological isomorphism from E₁ × E₂ to E.

name: Quotient TVS
description: For a closed subspace F of a TVS E, the quotient E/F with the quotient topology is again a TVS, and E/F is Hausdorff if and only if F is closed.

name: Product of TVS
description: The Cartesian product Πᵢ Eᵢ of TVS equipped with the product topology is again a TVS, and it is locally convex (resp. complete) if each factor is.

name: Minkowski functional (gauge)
description: For a convex absorbing set C containing 0, the Minkowski functional is p_C(x) = inf{λ > 0 : x ∈ λC}, which is a sublinear function and a seminorm when C is balanced.

name: Strict separation theorem
description: If A is a closed convex set and B is a compact convex set in a locally convex space with A ∩ B = ∅, then there exists a continuous linear functional strictly separating them: sup_{a∈A} f(a) < inf_{b∈B} f(b).

name: Supporting hyperplane theorem
description: At every boundary point of a closed convex set in a locally convex space, there exists a closed hyperplane containing the point and having the convex set on one side.

name: Bipolar theorem
description: For a subset A of a locally convex space, the bipolar A°° equals the closed convex balanced hull of A.

name: Space of continuous linear maps L(E, F)
description: The vector space of all continuous linear maps from a TVS E to a TVS F, which can be given various topologies depending on the notion of convergence desired.

name: Topology of bounded convergence (strong topology on L(E,F))
description: The topology on L(E,F) of uniform convergence on bounded subsets of E, making L(E,F) into a locally convex space when F is locally convex.

name: Topology of pointwise convergence (weak topology on L(E,F))
description: The coarsest topology on L(E,F) making all evaluation maps u ↦ u(x) continuous, also called the simple topology.

name: Topology of compact convergence
description: The topology on L(E,F) of uniform convergence on compact subsets of E, intermediate between pointwise and bounded convergence.

name: Barrelled space
description: A locally convex space in which every barrel (closed, convex, balanced, absorbing set) is a neighborhood of zero; every Fréchet space and every Baire locally convex space is barrelled.

name: Barrel
description: A subset of a TVS that is closed, convex, balanced, and absorbing.

name: Weak-* topology σ(E', E)
description: The weak topology on the dual E' of a TVS E induced by the duality ⟨E', E⟩, under which E' is a locally convex space and E embeds canonically into (E')'.

name: Mackey topology τ(E, F)
description: The finest locally convex topology on E consistent with the duality ⟨E, F⟩, defined as the topology of uniform convergence on σ(F, E)-compact convex balanced subsets of F.

name: Semi-reflexive space
description: A locally convex space E is semi-reflexive if the canonical map J: E → E'' is surjective (algebraic isomorphism), without requiring it to be a homeomorphism.

name: Strong topology β(E', E)
description: The topology on E' of uniform convergence on all bounded subsets of E, making E' a locally convex space called the strong dual.

name: Grothendieck completion theorem
description: Every Hausdorff locally convex space has a completion that is unique up to topological isomorphism, constructed as a subspace of the algebraic dual of E' with the topology of uniform convergence on equicontinuous sets.

name: Transpose (adjoint) of a continuous linear map
description: For u: E → F continuous linear, the transpose ᵗu: F' → E' is defined by ⟨ᵗu(f), x⟩ = ⟨f, u(x)⟩, and ᵗu is continuous for the weak-* and strong topologies.

name: Weak compactness and completeness
description: In a complete locally convex space, a closed bounded set is weakly compact if and only if every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.

name: Parallelogram law
description: In an inner product space, ‖x+y‖² + ‖x-y‖² = 2(‖x‖² + ‖y‖²), and a normed space satisfying this identity is an inner product space (Jordan-von Neumann theorem).

name: Orthogonality
description: Two elements x, y of an inner product space are orthogonal (x ⊥ y) if ⟨x,y⟩ = 0; a set S is orthogonal if its elements are pairwise orthogonal.

name: Orthogonal projection theorem
description: For every closed subspace M of a Hilbert space H, each x ∈ H has a unique decomposition x = m + m⊥ with m ∈ M and m⊥ ∈ M⊥, and m is the unique best approximation of x from M.

name: Orthonormal system
description: A family (eᵢ) in a Hilbert space such that ⟨eᵢ, eⱼ⟩ = δᵢⱼ (Kronecker delta), i.e., pairwise orthogonal unit vectors.

name: Normal operator
description: A bounded linear operator T on a Hilbert space satisfying T*T = TT*, implying the spectral theorem applies.

name: Direct sum of Hilbert spaces
description: The Hilbert space direct sum ⊕ᵢ Hᵢ consists of families (xᵢ) with xᵢ ∈ Hᵢ and Σᵢ ‖xᵢ‖² < ∞, equipped with the inner product ⟨(xᵢ),(yᵢ)⟩ = Σᵢ ⟨xᵢ,yᵢ⟩.
